procedure.description: posterior lumbar interbody fusion, L4-L5, with decompression

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 22630 (posterior lumbar interbody fusion, L4-L5, with decompression) with date of service 2026-08-02. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not demonstrate instability requiring fusion; decompression alone would be the covered procedure.

criteria.text: Failure of at least 12 months of conservative treatment including physical therapy, anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication, activity modification, and at least one epidural steroid injection.

Imaging documenting segmental instability or spondylolisthesis at the level to be fused: anterolisthesis of 3 millimeters or more, or translation of 4 millimeters or more or angulation of 10 degrees or more on flexion-extension radiographs, with stenosis or radiculopathy correlating with the symptoms.
Symptoms and examination findings correlate with the imaging level: radicular leg pain or neurogenic claudication with a corresponding dermatomal deficit.
Psychosocial screening completed with no untreated major depression or active substance use disorder, and nicotine-free or documented cessation of at least 6 weeks.

chart.text: Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

62 year old man in spine clinic with low back and leg pain going back about 2 years, much worse this past year. Drives a delivery route. Reviewed the imaging with him and the options from more therapy to decompression to fusion. His history otherwise: reflux on omeprazole as needed, anxiety, sees a counselor. Allergies: codeine makes him sick. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works retail. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. He has been on meloxicam 15 daily and gabapentin 600 three times daily, stopped lifting at work, and did a course of PT last year. Bilateral leg pain into the lateral calves and the tops of the feet with standing and walking, walks about 200 feet before he has to sit, better leaning on the cart. L5 distribution. Extensor hallucis longus 4 out of 5 on the left, reflexes symmetric, straight leg raise negative.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Spine PT evaluation. Flexion-based program, core stabilization, nerve glides. Plan 12 weeks, twice a week.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports slight improvement that does not last.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports slight improvement that does not last.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports about the same.
Fluoroscopically guided transforaminal epidural steroid injection, L4-L5 left. Tolerated well.
Second transforaminal epidural steroid injection, L4-L5 left. The first gave about 2 weeks of relief.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Back to decide. Symptoms unchanged, walking distance down to about 150 feet. Recommended L4-L5 decompression and interbody fusion given the slip and the motion on the films. Risks reviewed at length. Vitals today 126 over 87, pulse 76. Finished 12 weeks of PT, two epidurals with transient relief only, still on the meloxicam and gabapentin. That is 16 months of conservative care without durable benefit. PHQ-9 score 7, no substance use, never smoked. Realistic expectations about what fusion will and will not fix.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.3, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 185, LDL 132, HDL 45, triglycerides 128. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
He called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told him the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Here with a cough and congestion for 5 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, he remains sure about going ahead.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 14 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.
Pre-op. Medical clearance in the chart, A1c 6.1, stopped the meloxicam. Consent signed for L4-L5 posterior lumbar interbody fusion with instrumentation.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (instability); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
